project.objective: Determine whether Jahue B Burton's wife, shown in FamilySearch as Mary Ann Eastham, was truly the woman named Polly Burton in the census records, or whether these are two different people who were incorrectly merged on FamilySearch.
project.title: Jahue Burton's wife identity

questions.question: Do independent records confirm or refute that the woman recorded as Mary A./Polly Burton in the 1850–1880 census records as Jahue B. Burton's wife in Pulaski County, Kentucky, is the same individual as Mary Ann Eastham, shown on the FamilySearch profile as Jahue B. Burton's wife?
questions.rationale: Every fact about I2 (Mary Ann Eastham) derives solely from the FamilySearch collaborative tree (S1, quality 1 — compiled, unsourced). The census records already attached to Jahue B. Burton (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880) show his wife variously as 'Mary A Burton' and 'Polly Ann Burton' in Pulaski County; the FamilySearch profile assigns her birth surname 'Eastham' and a Greenup County, KY birth origin. After Jahue's 1898 death in Pulaski County, the profile places his wife in Boyd County (1900 residence, 1904 death, Fields Cemetery burial) — a geographically separate trajectory that raises a real possibility the FamilySearch profile merged two distinct women into one entry. Kentucky marriage records, Pulaski and Boyd county vital and probate records, and death/obituary sources can test whether a single woman's life history runs through both name forms and both counties, or whether the evidence supports two separate identities.

questions.question: Do independent records confirm or refute that the woman recorded as Jahue B Burton's wife in Pulaski County, Kentucky census records from 1850 through 1880 — variously listed as 'Mary A Burton' and 'Polly Burton' — is the same individual as Mary Ann Eastham, born circa 1823 in Greenup County, Kentucky?
questions.rationale: The FamilySearch Couple link between Jahue B Burton and Mary Ann Eastham rests entirely on the compiled FamilySearch Family Tree (quality 1), which has no independent source records attached to the Mary Ann Eastham persona. Census records 1850–1880 name Jahue's wife in Pulaski County as 'Mary A Burton' (1850, 1860) and 'Polly Ann / Polley A. P. Burton' (1870, 1880) — 'Polly' being a common diminutive of Mary. However, the birthplace data attached to I2 (Greenup County, northeastern KY) sits far from Pulaski County (south-central KY), and I2's death and burial are in Boyd County (also northeastern KY), raising the possibility that two women were incorrectly merged. Kentucky marriage records, early Greenup and Boyd County records, and Eastham family documentation are the primary avenues to confirm or refute the identity claim independently of the FamilySearch merge.

items.rationale: A marriage record for Jahue B. Burton is the single highest-priority source for this question: it would name the wife's maiden surname directly. Jahue was born 1818 and his eldest known child was born 1844, placing the marriage roughly 1836-1844. The Kentucky County Marriages collection (1804888, 3.38 million records) covers Pulaski County from 1799 and is indexed. Per loc_001, Pulaski County had a courthouse fire of unknown scope; published marriage transcriptions (1787-1860, 1798-1910) should be checked as backup if the index shows no result. If this search yields a maiden surname other than Eastham, that is strong evidence against the FamilySearch merger.

If Jahue's marriage is not found in Pulaski County, Greenup County is the next jurisdiction to search: marriages sometimes took place in the bride's home county rather than the groom's. If the FamilySearch merger is correct, Mary Ann Eastham's family was in Greenup County (her claimed birthplace), making a Greenup County marriage plausible. The Kentucky County Marriages collection (1804888) covers Greenup County from 1803 with 80-83% name-indexing per loc_002.

The 1850 census record for Jahue B. Burton is already attached to his profile on FamilySearch (record ARK M65K-9GS; a second entry M65V-BSV also exists). These records have not yet been extracted as assertions in this project. Reading them will capture the wife's given name, age, and — critically — her stated birthplace. If the birthplace is Kentucky or Greenup County, that is consistent with the Mary Ann Eastham merger; if it is a different state or county, that contradicts it. Wife is listed as 'Mary A Burton' in the indexed title.

The 1860 census record for Jahue B. Burton (ARK MZBZ-6GQ) is already attached on FamilySearch but not yet extracted as assertions. The wife is listed as 'Mary A Burton'. Reading this record will supply her age and birthplace as recorded in 1860, offering a second data point on her origin. Comparing the stated ages and birthplaces across census years will reveal whether the wife's profile is internally consistent — and whether it aligns with a woman born c.1823 in Greenup County, KY.

The 1870 census record (ARK MX4M-62D) is already attached on FamilySearch but unextracted. Notably the indexed title names her 'Polly Ann Burton' — the first census year where the 'Polly' form appears. Reading this record will capture her stated age and birthplace. If she is listed with initials or a middle name that expands 'A.P.' (as the 1880 record shows), that could clarify the name puzzle. The shift from 'Mary A.' to 'Polly Ann' between 1860 and 1870 is a pattern worth documenting.

The 1880 census record (ARK MCZP-VY3) is already attached on FamilySearch but unextracted. The indexed title gives the wife's name as 'Polley A. P. Burton' — initials 'A. P.' rather than just 'Ann'. Reading the original image will reveal what those initials stand for. The 1880 census also records each person's birthplace AND both parents' birthplaces — this is the most informative census year for establishing geographic origin. If the wife's parents' birthplaces are recorded, they may confirm or contradict the Greenup County Eastham family connection.

The FamilySearch profile for I2 (Mary Ann Eastham) places her death on 24 September 1904 in Boyd County. A 1904 death falls within Kentucky's 1892-1910 county-level death registration window (per loc_003), so a death register entry should exist. The Kentucky Deaths and Burials collection (1674848) covers Boyd County. If found, the death record may name the informant, the deceased's parents, spouse, birthplace, and place of burial — any of which could confirm or refute the identity merger. If the record names a spouse other than Jahue B. Burton (who died in 1898), that would strongly support the view that FamilySearch merged two different people.

The FamilySearch profile for I2 places her in Cannonsburg, Boyd County in 1900 — two years after Jahue's death in Pulaski County. Searching the 1900 census for Boyd County (specifically Cannonsburg or its township) for a widow named Burton, or for any woman named Mary Ann or Polly Eastham/Burton, will either confirm this residence or show it belongs to a different woman entirely. The 1900 census records both the number of years married and the number of children born/surviving — details that could align with or contradict the Pulaski County household. This is also a FAN check: if a Mary Ann Eastham is found in Boyd County in 1900 living with relatives named Eastham rather than Burton, that strongly supports two separate women.

Jahue B. Burton died 16 October 1898 in Pulaski County. His estate file — an administration bond, inventory, or settlement — would name his widow and heirs. If the widow is named 'Mary Ann' or 'Polly' Burton (without the Eastham surname), the record establishes her as the surviving wife of record in Pulaski County. The Kentucky Probate Records collection (1875188) covers Pulaski County from 1727. This is also directly relevant as a FAN record: the estate names the children, which can be cross-checked against the children already in the tree, confirming or adding to what we know about the family. The date window extends to 1910 because estate settlements sometimes took years to close. Bounds set by Jahue's death (1898) as creator.

The FamilySearch profile places I2's burial at Fields Cemetery, Princess, Boyd County, Kentucky. A FindAGrave or BillionGraves search for this cemetery may produce a headstone photograph with birth year, death year, and possibly the woman's full name or maiden name. A headstone reading 'Mary Ann Eastham Burton' would support the merger; one reading a different surname or naming a different spouse would support two separate women. This is an external-site search to be executed via search-external-sites.

FAN cluster search — Robert Eastham (b. ~1823-25, KY) appeared in the Burton household in BOTH the 1850 and 1860 censuses alongside Mary A. Burton. His recurring presence strongly suggests he is the wife's brother or close relative. Searching for Robert Eastham's own 1870 household will reveal: (1) his father's and mother's birthplaces from the 1880 census column if found there, (2) his own stated age/birthplace confirming identity, and (3) potentially his wife's and children's names/birthplaces — all of which can confirm or deny the Eastham family's Virginia origin consistent with Polley A.P. Burton's father born in Virginia per the 1880 census image. At least one FAN item is required for an identity question under BCG GPS Standard 14.

FAN cluster search — fallback if Robert Eastham is not found in the 1870 census. The 1880 census records father's and mother's birthplaces for every person. If Robert Eastham (b. ~1823-25 KY) is found in 1880, his father's birthplace column would directly confirm or deny whether the Eastham family came from Virginia — matching or contradicting Polley A.P. Burton's father's stated Virginia birthplace from the 1880 census image.

conflicts.description: Robert Eastham Jr.'s mother's birthplace: Virginia (1880 census image, a_144) vs. Kentucky (1870 marriage bond self-report, a_159)
conflicts.independence_analysis: The two assertions draw on distinct record events created by different informants at different times. a_144 is a 1880 census enumeration in which an unknown household member reported Robert's parents' birthplaces to an enumerator; a_159 is Robert's sworn self-declaration on a 1870 marriage bond in which he personally stated his mother was born in Kentucky. The records are independent — neither was copied from the other, and they were created a decade apart. Both ultimately rely on Robert's personal knowledge of his own family origins, but the quality of transmission differs: the census entry is oral statement filtered through an enumerator and recorder, while the bond is Robert's direct written declaration.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Under GPS evidence-weighing principles, a contemporary sworn self-report on a legal document carries greater weight than a retrospective census entry made by an unknown informant. a_159 (1870 marriage bond) is primary information: Robert personally swore the statement on a legal instrument and is the most proximate source for facts about his own parentage. a_144 (1880 census) is secondary information: the reporter is unknown, the enumeration is retrospective, and census entries for parents' birthplaces are routinely less reliable than sworn legal statements. The bond is also closer in time to the events it describes. Additionally, the a_159 value (Mother=Kentucky) aligns with Polley A.P. Burton's 1880 census parental birthplace record (Mother=Kentucky), corroborating the sibling hypothesis (h_002) that Robert Jr. and Polley Burton share a common Virginia-born father and Kentucky-born mother.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: a_159 (Robert's sworn self-report on the 1870 marriage bond: Mother born Kentucky) is accepted over a_144 (1880 census by unknown informant: Mother born Virginia). Primary sworn self-report on a legal instrument outweighs secondary retrospective census entry by unknown informant.

hypotheses.claim: Polly Burton (Mary A. Burton, Polley A.P. Burton) — Jahue B. Burton's wife shown in the 1850–1880 census records in Pulaski County, Kentucky — is a different person from Mary Ann Eastham, who married Ephriam Boggs in Greenup County, Kentucky on 30 January 1844. The FamilySearch profile LYYX-DS1 incorrectly merges these two distinct women.
hypotheses.notes: Primary hypothesis for q_001. The Boggs/Eastham marriage record (src_005, a_115) provides direct evidence of a separate Mary Ann Eastham who married Ephriam Boggs on 30 January 1844 in Greenup County — a woman who cannot simultaneously be Jahue Burton's wife Polly in Pulaski County. The 'Father of the Bride' Robert Eastham named in that marriage record (a_117) must have been born approximately 1795-1805 to have a daughter old enough to marry in 1844, making him too old to be the Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County) who co-resided with the Burtons in 1850 and 1860. Four census records consistently name Jahue's wife as Mary A. or Polly Burton but never state an Eastham maiden name, providing negative evidence against the FamilySearch merger. The 1880 census image of the Burton household (log_021) documents Polley A.P. Burton's father as Virginia-born and her mother as Kentucky-born; these facts are recorded in the log entry but no formal assertions have yet been extracted from that image, so no assertion IDs for those parental birthplace facts are available here.

hypotheses.claim: Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County, Kentucky; co-resident in the Jahue B. Burton household in Pulaski County in both the 1850 and 1860 censuses; married Margaret Rucker in Boyd County, Kentucky, 25 January 1870) is a sibling of Polley A.P. Burton (Jahue B. Burton's wife), both being children of a Virginia-born Eastham father and a Kentucky-born mother. This accounts for both Polley's possible Eastham maiden name and Robert Jr.'s persistent co-residence with the Burton family.
hypotheses.notes: Supporting hypothesis that would explain Robert Eastham Jr.'s appearance in two consecutive Burton census households while bearing a different surname. Key supporting pattern: Robert's sworn 1870 marriage bond (a_157, a_159) reports his father born in Virginia and his mother born in Kentucky. The 1880 Burton household census image (log_021) records Polley A.P. Burton's father born in Virginia and her mother born in Kentucky — an exact match with Robert's sworn self-report. However, no formal assertions have yet been extracted from log_021 for Polley's parental birthplaces; those facts exist only in the log entry notes and cannot be cited by assertion ID here. Open conflict on Robert's mother's birthplace: a_144 (Robert's 1880 census image, log_030, unknown household respondent) lists his mother as born in Virginia, directly contradicting a_159 (Robert's sworn 1870 marriage bond) which gives Kentucky. The bond is analytically superior — sworn self-report on an original document — versus a census entry from an unknown respondent with secondary knowledge. This conflict has not yet been formally registered in the conflicts[] section and remains open. NOTE on a_159 informant_bias_notes: those notes contain an error stating the conflict is with 'Polley A.P. Burton's 1880 census which shows the mother born in Virginia.' In fact the Burton 1880 census image (log_021) shows Polley's mother born in KENTUCKY. The real conflict is between Robert's own 1880 census (a_144, Virginia) and Robert's own 1870 bond (a_159, Kentucky). This error in the existing assertion should be corrected in a future assertions-only update.

# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1820-1905)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 10 December 1798 from Lincoln and Green Counties
- **County seat:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky (admitted 1792); before 1798, Lincoln and Green Counties
- **Economy:** Agriculture (tobacco, livestock), timber
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Presbyterian
- **Key events:** Civil War divided county loyalties

## Boundary changes
Stable within the 1820-1905 period. Before 10 December 1798, records are in Lincoln or Green County.

## Available record types

### Vital records
- County-level births/deaths required 1852-1862, 1874-1878, 1892-1910 only; statewide from 1911. County marriages from 1799; statewide marriages from 1958. Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- Marriage bonds from 1799; county birth/death registers for the windows above (sporadic)
- **Gap:** Pulaski listed in FamilySearch burned counties table; scope of courthouse fire loss unknown
- **Alternatives:** Church records, family Bibles, probate, mortality schedules

### Church records
- Baptist, Methodist, Presbyterian dominant
- Mostly not digitized; held by individual congregations and denominational archives
- Diocese of Lexington for Catholic records

### Census records
- Federal census 1820-1900 (1890 largely destroyed nationally); highly indexed at FamilySearch and Ancestry
- No state censuses in Kentucky
- Mortality schedules 1850-1880 list deaths in the census year

### Probate and court records
- Probate from 1801; circuit court from the early 1800s
- 102 digitized volumes at FamilySearch (first page only examined); includes will books and marriage records 1799-1955
- Will books and court minutes name heirs with relationships and ages

### Land records
- Metes and bounds system; Commonwealth of Kentucky issued grants
- County deed books from 1799; County Clerk holds records

### Military records
- Civil War service/pension at NARA (Atlanta region); Confederate pensions at Kentucky State Archives

### Cemetery, newspaper, tax records
- FindAGrave and BillionGraves for cemeteries; Newspapers.com/GenealogyBank for local papers; tax lists from 1799 at Kentucky State Archives

## Repository guide
- **FamilySearch (free):** Marriages, census, probate, church records (see Kentucky-wide collections)
- **Ancestry (subscription):** Federal census, Civil War records, land grants, newspapers
- **Pulaski County Clerk, Somerset:** Original records from 1799 (some lost in fire) — in-person/mail
- **Kentucky State Archives, Frankfort:** Vital records from 1911, tax lists, Confederate pensions
- **NARA Atlanta:** Federal Civil War and naturalization records

## Records NOT online
- Pre-1852 births and deaths (no civil registration before 1852)
- Records destroyed in courthouse fire
- Most individual church congregation records

## Known record losses
Pulaski County courthouse fire destroyed unknown records; date and scope not stated in FamilySearch Wiki.

## Research tips
- Start with Kentucky, County Marriages, 1786-1965 (collection 1804888) at FamilySearch — 3.38M indexed records
- Check published marriage transcriptions (1787-1860, 1798-1910) as backup for fire losses
- Use probate will books as vital-record substitutes; estate files name heirs with relationships
- Search adjoining counties: Casey, Laurel, Lincoln, McCreary, Rockcastle, Russell, Wayne
- Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) | [Kentucky Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)

# Locality Guide: Greenup County, Kentucky (1820-1905)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 12 December 1803 from Mason County; county seat Greenup
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Mason County (before 1803)
- **Economy:** Ohio River commerce, iron furnaces (Hanging Rock Iron Region), timber, railroads
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Disciples of Christ, Presbyterian
- **Key events:** 1937 Ohio River flood caused a courthouse disaster; Civil War border-county with Ohio

## Boundary changes
- Before 12 December 1803: territory was Mason County — all records there
- 16 February 1860: Boyd County carved from northeastern Greenup — pre-1860 Boyd-territory records are in Greenup County

## Available record types

### Vital records
- County-level births/deaths 1852-1862, 1874-1878, 1892-1910; statewide from 1911. County marriages from 1803. Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)

- Baptist, Methodist, Disciples of Christ
- FamilySearch holds Greenup, Kentucky, Church Records, 1829-1908 — **browse-only: 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable; must be examined image by image**
- Most congregation records remain with local churches or denominations

- Federal census 1820-1900 (1890 largely destroyed); Greenup County volumes are among the 24 fully examined digitized volumes at FamilySearch — most years highly indexed
- No state censuses in Kentucky

### Probate and court records
- Probate from 1837; court records from 1803
- Will books 1822-1895 at FamilySearch — **full-text searchable but not name-indexed**
- 1937 disaster may have damaged some volumes

### Land records
- Metes and bounds; county deed books from 1811; County Clerk, Greenup

### Military, cemetery, newspaper records
- Civil War service/pension at NARA; FindAGrave for cemeteries; Ashland Daily Independent (adjacent Boyd County) covered Greenup area; pre-1922 issues on microfilm at Kentucky Historical Society

## Repository guide
- **FamilySearch (free):** Marriage bonds, census, will books, church records, county birth/death/marriage registers

- Pre-1852 births and deaths (no civil registration)
- Records lost in the 1937 courthouse disaster
- Most individual church congregation records
- Church records volume 1829-1908 is browse-only

## Known record losses
- 1937 Ohio River flood caused courthouse disaster; unknown portion of pre-1937 records lost. Contact County Clerk for specifics.

- For Eastham family: search marriage bonds 1803-1862 (80-83% indexed) first

# Locality Guide: Boyd County, Kentucky (1820-1905)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 16 February 1860 from Greenup, Carter, and Lawrence Counties; county seat Catlettsburg
- **Parent jurisdictions (pre-1860):** Primarily Greenup County for northeastern territory; Carter and Lawrence for other areas
- **Economy:** Iron, timber, railroads; Ashland as industrial center after 1865; Ohio River commerce
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Presbyterian; Catholic and Episcopal in Ashland
- **Key events:** Civil War (county formed just before it began); rapid post-war industrial growth

## Boundary changes
Formed 1860; stable since. All pre-1860 events in present Boyd County territory are in Greenup County records (primary), or Carter/Lawrence Counties.

## Available record types

### Vital records
- County-level births/deaths 1852-1862, 1874-1878, 1892-1910; statewide from 1911. Boyd County began its own records in 1860. A death in 1904 falls within the 1892-1910 county registration window. Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- Marriage bonds from 1860; FamilySearch County Marriages (1786-1965) covers Boyd County
- No courthouse disasters reported for Boyd County

### Church records
- Baptist, Methodist, Presbyterian; Catholic and Episcopal in Ashland
- Diocese of Lexington for Catholic records
- FamilySearch Kentucky Church Records (1818-1995) covers broadly; specific Boyd County congregations mostly not digitized

### Census records
- Federal census 1860-1900 (1890 largely destroyed); 41 digitized volumes found at FamilySearch (first page only examined)
- No state censuses in Kentucky

### Probate and court records
- From 1860; will books 1860-1962 and court minutes 1860-1869 digitized at FamilySearch
- A death around 1904 should generate an estate file if the deceased held property

### Land, military, cemetery, newspaper records
- Land records from 1860 (pre-1860 in parent counties); Civil War records at NARA
- FindAGrave and BillionGraves for cemeteries including Fields Cemetery
- Ashland Daily Independent: Ancestry obituary index 1922-1945, 1970-1973, 1998-2010; pre-1922 on microfilm at Kentucky Historical Society

## Repository guide
- **FamilySearch (free):** Marriage bonds, census, will books, county death/birth registers

- **Boyd County Library, Catlettsburg:** Local Kentucky Deaths Index database — contact library
- **Kentucky State Archives, Frankfort:** Vital records from 1911, Confederate pensions, tax lists
- **NARA Atlanta:** Federal Civil War service/pension records

## Records NOT online
- Pre-1860 Boyd territory records are in Greenup County (and partly Carter, Lawrence)
- Most individual church congregation records
- Ashland Daily Independent pre-1922 (microfilm only)

## Known record losses
No courthouse disasters identified for Boyd County.

## Research tips

- Pre-1860 records: search Greenup County — Boyd County did not exist
